item.title: Timing Issue at 202° – Symptoms, Confirmation, and Fix
item.description:
Prerequisite

After checking the thread path, needle orientation, and other common causes, a small number of machines may have a timing issue.
This problem is most likely to occur after a severe bird’s nest or thread jam.

1. Symptoms

If you observe any of the following, and thread path, needle direction, and tension are already confirmed correct:

  • Frequent needle breaks (bent or broken needle tips)
  • Rotary hook fails to catch the upper thread loop (skipped stitches)
  • Bobbin thread cannot be picked up (loops not formed)

If these symptoms persist despite correct thread path and needle orientation, check the timing.

item.title: Why Incorrect Needle Direction Causes Thread Breaks
item.description:
If your embroidery thread keeps breaking and the broken area looks fuzzy, frayed, or damaged, the problem may not be thread tension. In many cases, the cause is an incorrectly installed needle or incorrect needle direction. author: Kimi Embroidery Repair Tech Station

Symptoms

You may notice one or more of the following:

  • The upper thread breaks repeatedly during embroidery.
  • The thread break point looks fuzzy or worn out.
  • The thread appears to be cut or scraped instead of cleanly broken.
  • The same needle position keeps causing thread breaks.
  • Adjusting thread tension does not solve the problem.

item.title: How to Adjust Belt Tension
item.description:
How to Adjust Belt Tension

The belt system plays an important role in controlling the movement of the embroidery frame and machine components.

Over time, belts may become loose due to long-term operation, temperature changes, or normal wear. Incorrect belt tension can affect embroidery accuracy and machine performance.

When Should You Adjust Belt Tension?

Belt tension adjustment may be needed when you notice:

  • Abnormal noise during machine operation
    Loose or improperly tensioned belts may create unusual sounds while the machine is running.

item.title: Computer Cannot Detect the SmartStitch Machine — Check Settings
item.description:
Computer Cannot Detect the SmartStitch Machine — Check Settings

One of the most frustrating issues in digital embroidery is when your computer simply does not recognise the SmartStitch machine. This prevents design transfer, parameter adjustments, and real‑time monitoring.

Most detection failures are not hardware‑related – they originate from incorrect settings, driver conflicts, or cable/port issues. Follow this structured troubleshooting process to quickly isolate and fix the problem.

Common Root Causes

  • Machine not powered on or in the wrong mode (e.g., offline / manual)
  • Faulty or loose USB/serial cable
  • Incorrect COM port or baud rate settings in the software
  • Outdated or missing USB drivers
  • Firewall or antivirus blocking the communication port
  • Multiple software instances accessing the same port
  • Damaged port on the computer or on the machine

Step‑by‑Step Diagnostic Process

Perform these checks in the recommended order – from the simplest to the most advanced.

item.title: How to Fix Bobbin Thread Showing on Top of Embroidery
item.description:
How to Fix Bobbin Thread Showing on Top of Embroidery

The upper thread tension is too tight compared to the bobbin tension, which is why the bobbin thread is being pulled to the top. Please reduce the upper thread tension or increase the bobbin tension to balance them.

When the bobbin thread appears on the top side of an embroidery design, it usually means the thread tension balance is incorrect.

item.title: How to Replace the Thread Break Sensor
item.description:
How to Replace the Thread Break Sensor

The Thread Break Sensor is an important part of the embroidery machine’s thread detection system. It monitors the movement of the upper thread and helps the machine detect when the thread has broken, run out, or is not feeding correctly.

When the sensor detects a thread break, the machine can stop embroidery and alert the operator so the problem can be corrected before continuing.

item.title: How to Adjust Thread Trimming Parameters
item.description:
How to Adjust Thread Trimming Parameters

Proper thread trimming settings are important for maintaining embroidery quality and ensuring stable stitching after color changes or trims.

Incorrect trimming parameters may cause the following issues:

  • Thread tail too short after trimming
    The remaining thread tail is not long enough, causing the upper thread to easily pull out of the needle when embroidery starts again.

  • Thread tail too long after trimming
    Excess thread remains on the back of the embroidery, creating loose thread tails and affecting the finished appearance.
